Amortization to begin on June 1, 1937, and principal to be repaid within a maximum period of 50 years. Interest from June 1, 1937, at the rate of 2½% per annum for the first 20 years, but if railway net earnings amount to more than $200,000 a year, surplus to be used for increasing interest to a maximum of 5% and then for additional amortization. Security: The railway's revenues and the guarantee of the Ministry of Railways; besides $10,000,000 Third-term Railway Construction bonds out of the $120,000,000 railway loan. Duration 15 years.

Granted by a Chinese banking consortium at an interest rate of 10.8% per year. Repayable in 10 years, beginning 1937, in 20 semi-annual instalments, June 30 and December 31. Secured on $14,000,000 Nanking-Kiangsi Construction bonds.
Shanghai-Nanking Railway Double Tracking credit for line from Shanghai to Soochow, granted by the British and Chinese Corporation in May, 1937.
Apart from double tracking, funds are to be provided for relaying the entire line and obtaining new locomotives and modern signalling equipment.
